items.title: CLI license metadata conflicts with stated binary license

findings.title: CLI license metadata conflicts with stated binary license
findings.explanation: The CLI identifies its license as LGPL, whereas README.md lines 65–69 says the distributed CGAL-linked CLI binaries are GPLv3. The other CLI XML files have the same LGPL label, potentially misleading users about binary redistribution obligations.
findings.suggestion: Align the displayed CLI license metadata with the actual executable license and include the appropriate license notices in distribution materials.

items.title: Mesh repair discards input point and cell attributes

findings.title: Mesh repair discards input point and cell attributes
findings.explanation: The repaired polydata contains only rebuilt geometry; input point, cell, and field data arrays are not copied. Users processing models with scalar measurements, labels, or other attributes receive a mesh without those arrays.
findings.suggestion: Preserve or remap attributes where feasible, and explicitly warn users about arrays that cannot be retained across topology changes.

items.title: RepairMesh can report success for an open output

findings.title: RepairMesh can report success for an open output
findings.explanation: When repair cannot close an input surface, the CLI only logs a warning and returns success if the output writes, although its XML describes a closed output. A user can consequently mistake an open surface for a successfully repaired closed one.
findings.suggestion: Return an explicit failure for a nonclosed result, or clearly expose partial success and describe that closure is not guaranteed.

items.title: CLI XML metadata lists LGPL instead of BSD-3-Clause / GPLv3

findings.title: CLI XML metadata lists LGPL instead of BSD-3-Clause / GPLv3
findings.explanation: Each CLI XML descriptor declares `<license>LGPL</license>`, whereas `CMakeLists.txt` (lines 12) and `README.md` (lines 65-69) explicitly note that the CGAL algorithms used here (such as Polygon Mesh Processing and 3D Alpha Wrapping) are licensed under GPLv3+, making the resulting CLI binaries governed by GPLv3, while the extension source itself is 3-clause BSD (`LICENSE.txt`). This metadata mismatch in the CLI XML descriptors could confuse users inspecting the module help panel.
findings.suggestion: Update `<license>` in the seven `.xml` files to `BSD-3-Clause (source) / GPL-3.0-or-later (binary)` or `GPLv3` to match `README.md` and `CMakeLists.txt`.

items.title: No automated tests included for the CLI modules

findings.title: No automated tests included for the CLI modules
findings.explanation: The repository does not define automated CTest tests for the seven CLI modules. Adding simple baseline CLI invocation tests would help catch regressions on the Slicer build farm.
findings.suggestion: Consider adding `BUILD_TESTING` checks and basic `sem_add_test` / CTest tests for the CLI modules.

claude.reason: I read vespaRepairMesh.h, vespaRepairMesh.cxx, vespaBooleanOperation.cxx and vespaMeshSubdivision.cxx. The code does what it claims, and CGAL exceptions are caught. The weaknesses are ordinary robustness gaps. vespaBooleanOperation.cxx lines 40-50 fall back to the unrepaired mesh when the repaired one is not closed, and report this only on stderr. Lines 117-118 pass -1 to the filter if the operation string is unknown. vespaMeshSubdivision.cxx lines 37-48 never check that the input was read. vespaRepairMesh.cxx lines 38-41 write an output that is still open, with only a stderr warning. These are all ordinary bugs. The modules are CLI-only, so Python or GUI conventions such as observers and parameter nodes do not apply. I found nothing that justifies 'concern'.

gpt.reason: Inspected all seven CLI wrappers and the shared repair code. A concrete limitation is that mesh repair reconstructs only geometry: SlicerVESPA/vespaRepairMesh.h:198-201 says `vtkSmartPointer<vtkPolyData> repaired = vtkSmartPointer<vtkPolyData>::New();`, `repaired->SetPoints(outputPoints);`, `repaired->SetPolys(outputFaces);`, and `return repaired;`. Consequently input point/cell arrays, such as scalars, are not carried into the repaired output. Also, if repair leaves an open mesh, SlicerVESPA/vespaRepairMesh.cxx:38-46 warns `input mesh: mesh is not closed after repair.` but still writes the result and returns according to writer success, despite README.md:30 describing a closed manifold. These are non-blocking correctness limitations; the separate-process CLI wrappers otherwise have straightforward filter pipelines. I could not run Slicer or inspect the external VESPA filters, so their runtime behavior and end-to-end results remain unverified.

gemini.reason: The seven CLI modules in SlicerVESPA/ (vespaAlphaWrapping.cxx, vespaBooleanOperation.cxx, vespaIsotropicRemesher.cxx, vespaMeshSubdivision.cxx, vespaPatchFilling.cxx, vespaRepairMesh.cxx, vespaShapeSmoothing.cxx) and shared repair header (SlicerVESPA/vespaRepairMesh.h:1-206) are cleanly implemented using SlicerExecutionModel (SEMMacroBuildCLI with EXECUTABLE_ONLY in SlicerVESPA/CMakeLists.txt:19-59), running off the GUI thread as CLI executables, handling CGAL exceptions gracefully (vespaRepairMesh.h:121-166), checking input polyData validity (vespaBooleanOperation.cxx:57-69, vespaRepairMesh.cxx:25-30), and returning proper exit codes on write (writer->Write() ? 0 : 1). Soundness is 'ok'.
